evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'This should take about five to ten minutes of your time so that we can be able to build an accurate code. You can depend on, sounds good.' — framing present but rep doesn't wait for customer affirmation; customer responds 'Huh' (unclear acknowledgment) and rep moves directly into next question.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks 'do you have any concerns, or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call?' — but this comes after substantial probing has already started (availability check, property type confirmed). Customer responds 'Not at all. I just need a, a quote.'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep: 'And a typical back count based on the home size is fifteen to 25 boxes. Do you feel that you fall within that range?' Customer: 'Definitely.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives range ('between six to seven hours') and trip total ('$2,320') but does not explicitly anchor to typical one-bedroom timing before personalizing. Provides some personalization (two movers, truck, journey distance/floors) but estimate lacks a clear 'typical for this size' baseline stated upfront.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep fully discloses trip fee ($864), explains hourly rate ($104/hour per mover), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and states 'no hidden fees of any type, no credit card fees, no steri fees, no disassemble or reassembly fees.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or any equivalent check-in after giving the $2,320 estimate. Customer immediately volunteers 'that's a little cheaper than you guys' without the rep creating space for it.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep: 'Finally we have on time guarantee we value your time. So, if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' — covers discount terms in full.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep: 'We have no worry damage coverage included on the already we that you're paying us. We will provide up to $2,000 per move. That is to repair replace and reimburse for your items.' — covers $2,000 and that it's built-in, but does not explicitly state 'no deductible / no fine print.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. Moves directly from Two Promises into estimate discussion without confirming the promises landed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep transitions from estimate into 'would you still want me to send you the email quotation' without checking what's still concerning the customer.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked plainly. Rep offers 'would you still want me to send you the email quotation' — this is an implicit ask dressed as a logistics question, not 'Would you like our help with your move?'
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirms date (Monday, via email quotation), phone number (via email), addresses (both locations confirmed on-site), but does NOT confirm arrival window, crew size (mentioned in estimate but not confirmed as a booking detail), or crew notes about customer concerns. Partial at best.

top_strength: Rep delivered a comprehensive, transparent pricing explanation covering the hourly rate, trip fee, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments, and explicitly ruled out hidden fees — setting clear expectations upfront.
coaching_note: Never ask for the business: rep should have used 'Would you like our help with your move?' instead of offering to email a quote, and should have paused after the estimate for 'Does that feel fair?' to let the customer respond before backing away from the close.
